'''Michael Schemper''' is a biostatistician and an academic, serving as professor emeritus at the [[Medical University of Vienna]].

Schemper's research focuses on nonparametric estimation and testing methods, [[survival analysis]], and particularly [[Cox proportional hazards model|Cox regression models]], [[logistic regression]] models, and explained variation in statistical models. He has been awarded Lifetime Honorary Memberships by both the International Society for Clinical Biostatistics (ISCB) and the Austro-Swiss Region (ROeS) of the [[International Biometric Society|International Biometric Society (IBS)]]. According to [[Google Scholar]], his work has been cited more than 21,000 times.

==Education==
Schemper studied statistics at the [[University of Vienna|Vienna University]] from 1972 to 1977, earning an [[Master of Science|M.Sc.]] degree in 1976 and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1977. He later completed his [[Habilitation]] in [[Medical Statistics]] and Documentation at Vienna University in 1985.<ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://researcherprofiles.meduniwien.ac.at/backend/db_files/cv_661_697f8abc56c63.pdf|title=Michael Schemper|website=Medical University of Vienna|access-date=June 17, 2025}}</ref>

==Career==
Schemper's academic career started as a biostatistician in 1977 and as an associate professor from 1985 at the (former) Medical Faculty of Vienna University. He was a visiting associate professor at the [[University of Texas]] in [[Houston]], where he remained from 1987 to 1988. In 1991, he became a professor of clinical biostatistics at the Medical University of Vienna,<ref name=cv/> and later became an emeritus professor there.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Schemper, PhD |url=https://www.meduniwien.ac.at/web/en/forschung/researcher-profiles/researcher-profiles/detail/?res=michael_schemper&cHash=6e87babade3fb7d61d3f1eb0e2ee2b5c |website=Medical University of Vienna |access-date=June 25, 2025 |language=en}}</ref> In 1991, he founded the Institute of Clinical Biometrics at the Medical University of Vienna and remained its head until 2015.<ref>{{cite web |title=Institute of Clinical Biometrics |url=https://data-science.meduniwien.ac.at/en/institutes/clinical-biometrics/ |website=Medical University of Vienna |access-date=June 17, 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

==Research==
Schemper has authored more than 300 publications, which have collectively received over 21,000 citations. His work spans both the application of [[statistics]] in medical research and the development of biostatistical methods.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=2GXL2AIAAAAJ&hl=de|title=Michael Schemper - Google Scholar|website=Google Scholar|access-date=November 5, 2025}}</ref> His research has focused on quantifying the variation in outcomes explained by prognostic factors,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Momesso |first1=Denise P. |last2=Tuttle |first2=R.
